title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
summary: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$. Its coefficients enumerate bounded compositions and submultisets, give, after normalization, the probability mass function of a sum of independent discrete uniform random variables, and are the weight multiplicities…
